_comment: THE HOST/DEVICE codex32 SEAM, as a gate rather than a comment.
Until this file existed, the invariant lived only in prose, in
crates/me-cli/src/seal/record.rs ('The device's `codex32.New` has no such
narrowing'). Prose does not fail a build. This does.
THE INVARIANT: host_admits => device_admits. The host (`me`) packs only the
constellation ms1 PROFILE; the device (the seedhammer fork) displays any
BCH-valid codex32 it can engrave. Host being the narrower side is the SAFE
direction: everything the host will put in a payload, the device will read.
A row with host_admits=true and device_admits=false is the dangerous
direction and is what both tests exist to catch -- the host would have
packed a record the device refuses, i.e. an engraved backup that will not
load.
WHAT THE TWO VERDICTS MEAN, exactly:
host_admits   -- Rust: mnemonic_engrave::sysw::classify(s) == Class::Codex32Secret
device_admits -- Go:   sysw.Classify(s) == ClassCodex32Secret
Both are the sysw record classifier, so the two columns answer the same
question in the two languages. Neither is a claim about any other layer.
WHY THE HOST IS NARROWER. Constellation ms1 is a deliberate two-gate PROFILE
over BIP-93: the string length must be in ms-codec's VALID_STR_LENGTHS
[50, 56, 62, 69, 75] or VALID_MNEM_STR_LENGTHS [51, 58, 64, 70, 77], and then
the 4-character id must be `entr`. Plain BIP-93 at 128/256 bits lands on 48
and 74 characters -- the profile's extra tag byte is what shifts it. So the
48- and 74-character rows below are CORRECT BIP-93 and correctly not
constellation records; nothing here is owed a widening of either accept set.
THE ROW SET MUST KEEP ALL THREE SHAPES -- yes/yes, no/yes, no/no. Without a
yes/yes row, a mutation that refuses everything passes; without a no/no row,
one that admits everything passes.
THIS FILE IS SHARED, BYTE FOR BYTE. mnemonic-engrave is the primary
(crates/me-cli/testdata/codex32_seam_vectors.json); the seedhammer fork
carries a vendored copy at sysw/testdata/codex32_seam_vectors.json. Both
tests pin the SAME sha256 of this file as a literal, so the two copies
cannot drift without one of the two suites going red. To change a row:
1. edit this file
2. sha256sum crates/me-cli/testdata/codex32_seam_vectors.json
3. put that value in SEAM_VECTORS_SHA256 in
crates/me-cli/tests/codex32_seam.rs AND in seamVectorsSHA256 in the
fork's sysw/codex32_seam_test.go
4. copy the file to the fork
PROVENANCE is per row, in each row's `source`.

vectors.name: bip93-secret-128
vectors.source: BIP-93 test vector 1, the unshared 128-bit secret (id `test`). Verbatim from the fork's codex32/codex32_test.go TestBIPVector1. THE KNOWN DIVERGENCE: valid BIP-93, 48 characters, so outside the constellation profile's length sets.

vectors.name: bip93-secret-256
vectors.source: BIP-93 test vector 4, the unshared 256-bit secret (id `leet`, seed ffeeddccbbaa99887766554433221100 twice). Verbatim from the fork's codex32/codex32_test.go TestBIPVector4. THE KNOWN DIVERGENCE at the 256-bit size: 74 characters.

vectors.name: bip93-share
vectors.source: BIP-93 test vector 3, share `s` of a 2-of-3 split (threshold 3, id `cash`). Verbatim from the fork's codex32/codex32_test.go TestBIPVector3. A SHARE is not a constellation record at all -- it fails both gates, the length and the id.

vectors.name: constellation-entr-128
vectors.source: The repo's canonical 128-bit constellation ms1 fixture (crates/me-cli/tests/cli.rs MS1 and eight other sites). ms_codec::inspect reports tag `entr`, kind Entr, 16 payload bytes, checksum valid. Packs today: `me sysw pack` writes a payload from it.

vectors.name: constellation-entr-256
vectors.source: The 256-bit constellation ms1 of the bip84 `bacon`x24 bundle, emitted by `mnemonic bundle --group-size 0` (crates/me-cli/src/seal/mod.rs bip84()). ms_codec::inspect reports tag `entr`, kind Entr, 32 payload bytes, checksum valid.

vectors.name: entr-id-but-off-profile-length-90
vectors.source: MS1_90 in crates/me-cli/src/seal/record.rs -- a real 42-byte-seed codex32 generated in the fork by `head -c 42 /dev/zero | go run ./cmd/biptool seed -seedlen 42 -id entr`. THE ID IS `entr` AND IT STILL FAILS: 90 is in neither profile length set. This row is why the message may not blame the id alone. It is also the LAST length a seed plate's QR can carry, so the device admits it.

vectors.name: past-the-engraveable-cap-91
vectors.source: MS1_91 in crates/me-cli/src/seal/record.rs, same generator at -seedlen 43. One character past MAX_ENGRAVEABLE_MS1_LEN = 90, which BOTH sides apply (Rust RecordError::MsTooLong; Go sysw.MaxEngraveableMs1Len). An agreement row on the far side of the cap.

vectors.name: bip93-bad-checksum
vectors.source: BIP-93's own BAD-CHECKSUM vector, verbatim from the fork's codex32/codex32_test.go TestBIPBadChecksums (and codex32/polish_test.go, which pins Describe(err) == "bad checksum"). THE NEGATIVE CONTROL: neither side admits it, so a mutation that admits everything cannot pass.

vectors.name: preimage-plate-0x03
vectors.source: SPEC_ms_hashlock section 1, kind 0x03 with id `hash`: a hashlock PREIMAGE plate, produced by the H1 plan's gate-wired `ms hashlock` (mnemonic-secret 3592532, gate run 13); ms-codec 0.7 refuses it with `reserved-prefix byte was 0x03, expected 0x00` at exit 2 (that plan's downgrade row). NOT A SEED: cut as one it exposes a spend secret as a backup, loaded as one it derives keys from a hashlock preimage. H0 (SPEC_ms_hashlock section 9) makes it INERT on both sides -- never Codex32Secret, no class of its own -- and this row is the tripwire: it goes red on the host the day `me` bumps to ms-codec 0.8 without a refusing arm, and on the device if the prefix test is ever removed.

vectors.name: bip93-plain-payload-0x03
vectors.source: codex32.NewSeed("ms", 0, "test", 's', 16 bytes with byte 0 = 0x03): a plain BIP-93 unshared secret whose seed happens to begin 0x03. H0's device guard MUST leave it alone -- the preimage kind is an UNSHARED string with a 33-byte payload whose first byte is 0x03, and this payload is 16 bytes. Measured on the fork at 839fa5aa. Fidelity C-2 (hashlock-H0-plan-R0-r0-fidelity.md).

vectors.name: bip93-share-payload-0x03
vectors.source: codex32.NewSeed("ms", 2, "test", 'a', 33 bytes with byte 0 = 0x03): a 2-of-N SHARE whose SSS point begins 0x03. A share carries no kind byte (SPEC_ms_hashlock section 1 rule 2: the check is singles-only); H0 must not make it inert, or one such share would refuse a whole sealed payload as unreadable. Measured on the fork at 839fa5aa. Fidelity C-2.

vectors.name: preimage-shape-entr-id
vectors.source: codex32.NewSeed("ms", 0, "entr", 's', 33 bytes with byte 0 = 0x03): the preimage SHAPE (unshared, 33-byte payload, prefix 0x03) under the id `entr`. The kind is the prefix byte, not the id (SPEC_ms_hashlock section 1): ms-codec 0.7 refuses the prefix, 0.8 refuses the id/prefix mismatch (TagKindMismatch), and the device treats it as inert -- never a seed either way. Measured on the fork at 839fa5aa.

vectors.name: bip93-plain-33-byte-payload-0x03
vectors.source: codex32.NewSeed("ms", 0, "test", 's', 33 bytes with byte 0 = 0x03): THE COLLISION, and it is deliberate. A plain BIP-93 unshared secret whose 33-byte seed happens to begin 0x03 is byte-for-byte indistinguishable from a hashlock PREIMAGE plate -- the kind is the prefix byte (SPEC_ms_hashlock section 1), the payload width is the same, and the id is not consulted -- so H0 refuses it on both sides. This is CONVERGENCE, not a device narrowing: `me` refuses this exact string too (ms-codec 0.7 at the prefix gate, 0.8 as a TagKindMismatch), measured. The cost is bounded and known: a real 264-bit BIP-93 master seed beginning 0x03 (about 1 in 256 of 33-byte seeds) is refused rather than engraved. The 16-, 20-, 24-, 28- and 32-byte seeds are untouched, and so is every share -- see bip93-plain-payload-0x03 and bip93-share-payload-0x03, both device_admits: true. Consulting the id instead would engrave a mistagged REAL preimage as a seed (tests I-1), which is the worse failure: a refusal costs a re-encode, a wrong cut exposes a spend secret. Post-implementation review I-1/M-2 (agent-reports/hashlock-H0-post-impl.md).
